liebermann.description_de: Interpolator Henrici Huntendoniensis der Ausgabe von 1145
liebermann.shelfmark_as_given: The interpolator of Henry of Huntingdon’s Historia Anglorum (edition of 1145)
liebermann.laws: In Cn, Wl art, ECf retr
liebermann.notes: An interpolator of the 1145 edition of Henry of Huntingdon who, c. 1150–1200, inserted In Cn (to III 44, from dhu) into the history of Cnut; manuscripts Lb, sp (exemplar of S, Pl), Rc, Ct, Jo, Va, Pa, Sin. Perhaps the same person appended the Tripartita (Wl art, ECf retr) and the Genealogia Normannica to 1154.

entries.text_de: Interpolator Henrici Huntendoniensis der Ausgabe von 1145. Er schiebt c. 1150—1200 in dessen Geschichte Cnut's7 ein: In Cn bis III 44, u. S. 612, aus dhu. Vgl. die Hss.: Lb sp (Vorlage von S Pl) Rc Ct Jo Va Pa Sin. Vielleicht derselbe hängt der Chronik die Tripartita (s. d.) an, d. i. Wl art, u. S. 486, ECf retr, u. S. 627 und Geneal. Normann. bis 1154.
entries.text_en: Interpolator of Henry of Huntingdon, of the edition of 1145. C. 1150—1200 he inserts into Henry's history of Cnut7: In Cn up to III 44, below, p. 612, from dhu. Cf. the MSS: Lb sp (exemplar of S Pl) Rc Ct Jo Va Pa Sin. Perhaps the same man appends to the chronicle the Tripartita (see under that word), i.e. Wl art, below, p. 486, ECf retr, below, p. 627, and Geneal. Normann. to 1154.

transcription.doubts: Dash in '1150—1200' printed short (en-dash-like); kept as —. Letter-spacing of 'Tripartita' is slight but appears deliberate. A tiny low dot is printed between 'Rc' and 'Ct' ('Rc.Ct'), probably a stray mark of type; not transcribed.

others.text: O’Brien (2003): following Diana Greenway’s edition of Henry of Huntingdon (Oxford 1996), the Instituta was interpolated into the fifth edition, version B, of the Historia by c. 1190 (the hypearchetype was probably written in 1149). Its copies form several branches, not Liebermann’s single row: Lb (O’Brien’s La); S with Pl, Vincent 98 and Harley 785; Ba with Va; J (Jo) with T.
